text:
Let's explore [[Identify equivalent fractions when presented as shapes or objects]]! You might feel that [[Thinks dimensions are needed to compare fractions]], but using a [[Fraction wall]] makes it easy. 

Look at a wall with rows for halves, thirds, quarters, sixths, eighths, and twelfths, all the same length. Find your fraction and trace straight down to rows that line up. Those exact matches are equivalent—their top and bottom numbers were both multiplied or divided by the same number. Adding or changing just one number breaks equivalence. Now, predict one more match and check it!
